title: Two fixed Fu water balances can exceed the single-curve bound on runoff slope loss under a uniform demand rise
abstract: We test whether a single Fu curve bound on runoff slope loss also holds for the sum of different hydrologic areas. An exact finite-change identity shows that it need not hold. The bound fails when the covariance of local fractional loss and runoff elasticity exceeds a nonnegative local penalty. In two fixed equal areas with the same rain and demand, Fu parameters 1.3 and 6, and a uniform 20% demand rise, mean runoff falls 10.95% and its rain slope falls 19.08%. Each area separately meets the single-curve bound. A uniform infinitesimal change also violates the aggregate bound. Of 8,075 retained constructed grid cases, 2,070 violate it; these counts are not real-catchment frequencies. High-precision derivatives and an exact identity check confirm the result. Thus the reported Australian slope-loss form cannot alone exclude spatial Fu evaporation changes. No observations were fitted. Broad parameter contrasts, large demand changes and an equilibrium model limit physical inference. The Australian cause remains open. Code, all constructed grid cases, proofs, audits and a figure are included.

display.caption: Constructed two-area water balances can lose more rain slope than mean runoff under one uniform demand rise. The cross is an attributed prior regional estimate, not a fit.
